title: PR #518: confirm payments by webhook
summary: create_order no longer blocks on the gateway capturing the payment. It creates a payment intent, saves the order as pending and returns 202. A new webhook handler marks the order paid and sends the receipt when the gateway reports success.
other: Order gains intent_id; status gains the value 'pending' (shop/orders.py)
No test covers the webhook arriving before the order is saved

flows.title: Checkout to paid
flows.description: Triggered by the checkout page posting an order. Promises that a successful payment ends with the order marked paid and one receipt sent. Drawn as a sequence because the PR splits one blocking request into two requests from different actors, and correctness now depends on which one reaches the orders table first.

nodes.label: Checkout page
nodes.notes: Still treats any 2xx as paid and shows the thank-you screen. With 202 pending it must poll or say 'processing'.

nodes.label: Payment gateway
nodes.notes: External. Delivers payment.succeeded at least once, retries only on non-2xx, and can deliver within milliseconds of create_intent returning.

functions.change: marks order paid on payment.succeeded, enqueues receipt
notes: Race: the webhook can land before create_order has saved the order. find_by_intent returns None, the handler answers 200, the gateway never retries, and the order stays pending forever. Answer 5xx for an unknown intent, or save the order before calling create_intent.
No signature check on the webhook body: anyone can mark an order paid.
Not idempotent: a redelivered event enqueues a second receipt.
functions.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+def on_payment(event):
+    if event["type"] != "payment.succeeded":
+        return 200
+    order = find_by_intent(event["intent_id"])
+    if order is None:
+        return 200
+    order.status = "paid"
+    save_order(order)
+    queue.enqueue(send_receipt, order.id)
+    return 200
functions.label: on_payment()
find_by_intent()
